# Compliance Crosswalk and Verification

## OMB M-21-31 — the mandate that sets the floor

OMB M-21-31, *Improving the Federal Government's Investigative and Remediation
Capabilities Related to Cybersecurity Incidents*, defines four event-logging
maturity tiers and the retention each requires
([M-21-31](https://www.whitehouse.gov/wp-content/uploads/2021/08/M-21-31-Improving-the-Federal-Governments-Investigative-and-Remediation-Capabilities-Related-to-Cybersecurity-Incidents.pdf)).

| Tier | Meaning | Deadline |
|---|---|---|
| EL0 | Not effective — logging requirements of highest criticality not met | — |
| EL1 | Basic — highest-criticality requirements met | August 2022 |
| EL2 | Intermediate — intermediate-criticality requirements met | February 2023 |
| EL3 | Advanced — full enterprise-wide logging maturity | August 2023 |

Deadlines as recorded in the repo's
[federal ConMon gap roadmap](https://github.com/WhalerMike/uiao/blob/main/docs/customer-documents/orgcomp-series/federal-orgcomp-conmon-gap-roadmap.md).
All three have passed. An agency below EL3 today is not approaching a deadline;
it is carrying an open finding.

**EL1 retention floor: 12 months in active (readily accessible) storage plus
18 months in cold storage.** Under M-21-31 the logs are retained at the agency
and made available to CISA and the FBI on request
([federal ConMon reporting reference](../../uiao-orgcomp-integration/06-federal-conmon-reporting-reference.qmd)).

::: {.callout-important}
## The 90-day interactive window does not meet EL1 on its own

Vol III Book 06 configures a 90-day interactive tier plus archive for AU-11 /
NARA GRS 3.2, and explicitly records that this is **shorter than the M-21-31
EL1 active-storage floor**. It documents two conformant options: extend
interactive retention to 12 months for in-scope tables, or argue that the
Tier 2 archive's asynchronous query-job latency still satisfies "readily
accessible" for a given table and record the residual-risk acceptance.

**That decision is owned by
[Vol III Book 06 §AU-11 Retention Architecture](../../orgcomp-series/Vol_III_Book_06_OrgComp_SIEM_XDR_Detection.qmd), not by this
page.** What follows is the mechanism for implementing whichever option the
agency has recorded — per table, so an assessor can trace the choice.
:::

## Retention configuration {#retention}

Log Analytics retention is set **per table**, not on the workspace and not on
the diagnostic setting. Two values matter:

- `RetentionInDays` — the interactive (hot) window. Directly queryable.
- `TotalRetentionInDays` — interactive plus archive. Archive data requires a
  search job or restore to query.

```powershell
$WorkspaceRg   = "<resource-group>"
$WorkspaceName = "<workspace-name>"

# M-21-31 EL1 option 1: 12 months interactive (365d) + 18 months archive
# = 30 months total (913d) for the in-scope identity and audit tables.
$M2131Tables = @(
    "SigninLogs",
    "AADNonInteractiveUserSignInLogs",
    "AADServicePrincipalSignInLogs",
    "AADManagedIdentitySignInLogs",
    "AuditLogs",
    "AADProvisioningLogs",
    "MicrosoftGraphActivityLogs",
    "AzureActivity",
    "OfficeActivity",
    "SecurityAlert"
)

foreach ($Table in $M2131Tables) {
    Set-AzOperationalInsightsTable `
        -ResourceGroupName $WorkspaceRg `
        -WorkspaceName $WorkspaceName `
        -TableName $Table `
        -RetentionInDays 365 `
        -TotalRetentionInDays 913
}
```

Audit the applied state — this output is assessor evidence, not just an
operational check:

```powershell
Get-AzOperationalInsightsTable -ResourceGroupName $WorkspaceRg -WorkspaceName $WorkspaceName |
  Select-Object Name, RetentionInDays, TotalRetentionInDays,
    @{n='M2131_EL1'; e={ if ($_.RetentionInDays -ge 365 -and $_.TotalRetentionInDays -ge 913) { 'PASS' } else { 'REVIEW' } }} |
  Sort-Object M2131_EL1, Name | Format-Table -AutoSize
```

::: {.callout-warning}
## Three retention settings that look equivalent and are not

1. **`retentionPolicy` on the diagnostic setting** — applies to
   **storage-account destinations only**. It does nothing for a Log Analytics
   destination
   ([Azure Monitor REST reference](https://learn.microsoft.com/azure/data-factory/monitor-logs-rest#enable-diagnostic-logs-via-the-monitor-rest-api)).
2. **Workspace-level default retention** — the fallback for tables with no
   explicit setting. Silently governs any table you forget.
3. **Table-level retention** — the only one that reliably satisfies a
   per-table M-21-31 or AU-11 position.

Setting (1) and believing you have configured (3) is the most common
retention failure on this surface, and it fails at exactly the wrong moment:
during an incident, when someone queries beyond the real horizon and finds
nothing.

The M365 unified audit log is a fourth, separate regime entirely — governed by
Purview audit retention policies and license tier, not by any of the above.
See [M365 unified audit §Retention](03-m365-unified-audit.qmd#retention--the-tier-that-decides-the-evidence).
:::

## NIST SP 800-53 Rev 5 — control to category

| Control | Requirement | Categories that supply the evidence |
|---|---|---|
| **AU-2** Event Logging | Identify events the system is capable of logging and select those to be logged | All Entra core categories; activity log `Administrative` / `Security` / `Policy`; UAL content types |
| **AU-3** Content of Audit Records | Records contain what/when/where/source/outcome/identity | Native schema of each table; enforced downstream by the [SIEM adapter](../../adapter-specs/siem/siem.qmd) canonical claim shape |
| **AU-6** Audit Review, Analysis, Reporting | Review and analyze records for indications of inappropriate activity | Sentinel analytics rules and the review cadence in [Vol III Book 06](../../orgcomp-series/Vol_III_Book_06_OrgComp_SIEM_XDR_Detection.qmd) |
| **AU-11** Audit Record Retention | Retain per records-retention requirements | `RetentionInDays` / `TotalRetentionInDays`; Purview retention policy for the UAL |
| **AU-12** Audit Record Generation | Generate records for the AU-2 event set across all components | Diagnostic settings on **every** subscription and resource; Azure Policy enforcement |
| **SI-4** System Monitoring | Detect attacks and indicators of potential attacks | `AADUserRiskEvents`, `AADRiskyUsers`, `SecurityAlert`, activity log `Security` |
| **AC-2** Account Management | Monitor account creation, modification, enabling, disabling, removal | `AuditLogs`, `AADProvisioningLogs`, UAL `Audit.AzureActiveDirectory` |
| **AC-6** Least Privilege | Audit execution of privileged functions | `AuditLogs` (role assignment, PIM activation); activity log `Administrative` (Azure RBAC) |
| **IA-2** Identification and Authentication | MFA for privileged and non-privileged accounts | `SigninLogs` with `appliedConditionalAccessPolicies` — requires the `Policy.Read.All` grant described in [Entra ID](01-entra-id.qmd) |

::: {.callout-note}
## AU-12 is where estates actually fail

AU-2 asks whether you *selected* the right events. AU-12 asks whether records
are generated **across all system components**. A tenant with perfect Entra
diagnostic settings and eleven of fourteen subscriptions exporting activity
logs passes an AU-2 review and fails AU-12 — and the gap is invisible to every
query that only looks at what arrived. This is why
[Azure platform §Enforce at scale](02-azure-platform.qmd#part-3--enforce-at-scale-with-azure-policy)
treats the policy compliance percentage, not the ingestion query, as the
coverage metric.
:::

## FedRAMP — KSI-MLA indicators

The FedRAMP CR26 catalog's **Monitoring, Logging, and Auditing** theme
(`KSI-MLA`) is what this configuration is graded against under FedRAMP 20x.
Statements below are quoted from the catalog snapshot at
`src/uiao/canon/compliance/reference/fedramp-cr26/`.

| Indicator | Statement | Satisfied by |
|---|---|---|
| **KSI-MLA-LET** Logging Event Types | "A list of information resources and event types that will be logged, monitored, and audited is maintained and persistently reviewed to ensure these activities occur." | The category tables in pages 1–3, maintained as code, plus the verification scorecard below |
| **KSI-MLA-OSM** Operating SIEM Capability | "A SIEM or similar system(s) is used and persistently reviewed for centralized, tamper-resistant logging of events, activities, and changes." | Log Analytics / Sentinel as the central store; immutable archive per Vol III Book 06 |
| **KSI-MLA-RVL** Reviewing Logs | "Logs are persistently reviewed and audited." | Sentinel analytics rules and the AU-6 review cadence |
| **KSI-MLA-ALA** Authorizing Log Access | "A least-privileged, role and attribute-based, and just-in-time access authorization model is used and persistently reviewed for access to log data based on organizationally defined data sensitivity." | Workspace RBAC plus PIM on Log Analytics Reader / Sentinel roles |
| **KSI-MLA-EVC** Evaluating Configurations | "The configuration of machine-based information resources, especially infrastructure as code, is persistently evaluated and tested." | Azure Policy DINE assignments and the Bicep in pages 1–2 |

`LET` is the reason the *maintained list* matters as much as the
configuration. The indicator is not satisfied by having logging turned on; it
is satisfied by a reviewed, current inventory of resources and event types
that someone can show has been checked. The category tables in this section
are that inventory — kept in git, reviewed on the `lifecycle_review` cadence
in each page's frontmatter.

## CISA

| Driver | Relationship to this configuration |
|---|---|
| **SCuBA** secure configuration baselines | M365/Entra baseline assertions are assessed by ScubaGear, which reads tenant configuration — including whether diagnostic settings and unified audit logging are enabled. See the [`scubagear` adapter](../../adapter-specs/scubagear/scubagear.qmd). |
| **BOD 26-04** (risk-based remediation; revoked BOD 22-01) | Remediation deadlines are enforced against an asset inventory; exploitation detection depends on the device and identity telemetry emitted here. |
| **BOD 25-01** (M365 secure configuration) | Directly requires SCuBA baseline implementation and continuous assessment of M365 tenants. See [BOD 25-01 — close before assess](../../whitepapers/bod-25-01-close-before-assess.qmd). |
| **ZTMM v2.0** Visibility & Analytics pillar | Maturity in this pillar is a direct function of telemetry completeness. Signals the FedRAMP Moderate boundary blocks are enumerated in [`gcc-moderate-telemetry-gaps.yaml`](https://github.com/WhalerMike/uiao/blob/main/src/uiao/canon/data/gcc-moderate-telemetry-gaps.yaml). |

::: {.callout-warning}
## Some signals cannot be emitted at all under the boundary

26 telemetry signals are unavailable, restricted, or retention-limited under
the FedRAMP Moderate authorization boundary — mostly Microsoft's own
cloud-side computed products (risk scores, adoption aggregates, ML-derived
detections) rather than raw events. No amount of diagnostic-setting
configuration recovers them.

Do not write an SSP narrative claiming coverage this configuration cannot
deliver. The honest accounting, including which gaps an in-boundary Event Hubs
pipeline can partially rebuild, is
[Event Logging Under the GCC-Moderate Boundary](../../whitepapers/event-logging-fedramp-boundary-limitations.qmd).
:::

## The verification scorecard

One query, all three planes. Run daily; treat any `FAIL` as an AU-12 finding
until cleared.

```kusto
// UIAO SIEM emission scorecard — all three planes.
// FAIL = no data in 24h. Absent row = never emitted (worse).
let window = 24h;
let expected = datatable(TableName:string, Plane:string, Tier:string)
[
    "SigninLogs",                      "Entra",  "core",
    "AADNonInteractiveUserSignInLogs", "Entra",  "core",
    "AADServicePrincipalSignInLogs",   "Entra",  "core",
    "AADManagedIdentitySignInLogs",    "Entra",  "core",
    "AuditLogs",                       "Entra",  "core",
    "AADProvisioningLogs",             "Entra",  "core",
    "MicrosoftGraphActivityLogs",      "Entra",  "core",
    "AADRiskyUsers",                   "Entra",  "risk",
    "AADUserRiskEvents",               "Entra",  "risk",
    "AzureActivity",                   "Azure",  "core",
    "OfficeActivity",                  "M365",   "core",
    "SecurityAlert",                   "Signal", "core",
];
let observed = union withsource=TableName
        SigninLogs, AADNonInteractiveUserSignInLogs,
        AADServicePrincipalSignInLogs, AADManagedIdentitySignInLogs,
        AuditLogs, AADProvisioningLogs, MicrosoftGraphActivityLogs,
        AADRiskyUsers, AADUserRiskEvents,
        AzureActivity, OfficeActivity, SecurityAlert
    | where TimeGenerated > ago(window)
    | summarize Records = count(), LastRecord = max(TimeGenerated) by TableName;
expected
| join kind=leftouter observed on TableName
| extend Records = coalesce(Records, 0)
| extend Status = case(
      Records == 0,             "FAIL",
      LastRecord < ago(6h),     "STALE",
                                "PASS")
| project Plane, Tier, TableName, Status, Records, LastRecord
| order by Status asc, Plane asc, TableName asc
```

::: {.callout-note}
## A `union` over a table that has never existed

If a table has never received a single record it does not exist in the
workspace, and naming it in a `union` produces a semantic error rather than an
empty result. That is the failure mode this query is built around — the
`datatable` of expectations is joined against observations, so a table that
has never emitted shows as `FAIL` instead of breaking the query.

If the `union` itself errors on a workspace where several tables have never
existed, prefix the offending names with `union isfuzzy=true` for the
diagnostic run — then treat every fuzzed-away table as a `FAIL`, not as a
pass.
:::

## Assessor evidence pack

What to hand an assessor, and what each artifact proves:

| Artifact | Proves | Produced by |
|---|---|---|
| Entra diagnostic setting `GET` output | AU-2 category selection at the identity plane | `az rest --method GET` ([page 1](01-entra-id.qmd#path-c--az-rest)) |
| Azure Policy compliance report | AU-12 generation across all components | Azure Policy compliance dashboard |
| Table retention audit | AU-11 and M-21-31 EL1 retention position, per table | `Get-AzOperationalInsightsTable` ([above](#retention)) |
| `Get-AdminAuditLogConfig` output | UAL enabled at the tenant | Exchange Online PowerShell ([page 3](03-m365-unified-audit.qmd)) |
| Management API `subscriptions/list` | UAL content-type coverage | Management Activity API ([page 3](03-m365-unified-audit.qmd)) |
| 30 days of scorecard results | KSI-MLA-LET persistent review; continuous AU-2 coverage | The scorecard above, run on a schedule |
| Boundary-probe drift findings | Which gaps are boundary-imposed rather than misconfiguration | [GCC Boundary Probe adapter](https://github.com/WhalerMike/uiao/blob/main/src/uiao/adapters/modernization/gcc_boundary_probe/) |

The last row matters disproportionately. An assessor who finds a telemetry gap
will ask whether it is a control failure or an authorization-boundary
constraint. An agency that can produce the gap matrix and the probe findings
answers that in one document; an agency that cannot is defending a finding it
did not cause.

## Substrate integration

Emission configured per this section feeds the substrate as follows:

- The [`siem` adapter](../../adapter-specs/siem/siem.qmd) ingests the emitted
  events and normalizes them to canonical claim shape with a provenance
  envelope — the `AU-*` and `SI-4` evidence stream.
- The [GCC Boundary Probe](https://github.com/WhalerMike/uiao/blob/main/src/uiao/adapters/modernization/gcc_boundary_probe/)
  runs the completeness queries and emits `DRIFT-BOUNDARY` findings when a
  category stops emitting.
- The [Telemetry Modernization Spec](../../modernization-specs/telemetry/telemetry.qmd)
  imposes the ADR-006 determinism guarantees — no silent drops, append-only,
  ordered, idempotent — that the ingestion pipeline must honor.

Configuration without the probe is a point-in-time claim. The substrate's
position is that a compliance claim is only as good as the drift detection
behind it.
